results.name: Ankle Plantar Flexion
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and your hands resting on your hips or at your sides for balance..
Rise onto your toes, lifting your heels off the floor.
Lower your heels back to the starting position. Repeat the movement.
tips: Keep your knees slightly bent to reduce strain on your joints and enhance stability.
Use a mirror to check your form and ensure that your ankles are aligned properly.
Focus on maintaining a steady breathing pattern, exhaling as you rise and inhaling as you lower.
results.description: Ankle Plantar Flexion is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the calves (lower legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shins.

results.name: Arm Crossover Chest Out
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and your arms extended out to the sides at shoulder height, elbows bent and palms facing the floor.
Bring your arms forward while straightening them and cross them in front of your chest twice.
Return your arms to the starting position, extending them out to the sides and bringing your chest forward.
Continue crossing your arms in front of your chest and extending them back out to the sides in a controlled, rhythmic manner.
tips: Keep your shoulders relaxed to avoid unnecessary tension in your neck and upper back.
Use a mirror to ensure your movements are symmetrical and maintain proper form.
Breathe deeply, exhaling as you cross your arms and inhale as you extend them back out.
results.description: Arm Crossover Chest Out is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back.

results.name: Arm Crossover
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and your arms extended straight out to the sides at shoulder height, palms facing the floor.
Bring your arms forward and cross them in front of your chest.
Return your arms to the starting position, extending them out to the sides.
Continue crossing your arms in front of your chest and extending them back out to the sides in a controlled, rhythmic manner.
tips: Maintain an upright posture to avoid straining your back and neck.
Use a consistent pace to help coordinate your movements and keep them fluid.
Breathe steadily, exhaling as you cross your arms and inhaling as you extend them back out.
results.description: Arm Crossover is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back.

results.name: Arm Double Crossover
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and your arms extended out to the sides at shoulder height, elbows bent and palms facing the floor.
Bring your arms forward while keeping them bent and cross them in front of your chest twice.
Return your arms to the starting position, extending them out to the sides.
Continue crossing your arms in front of your chest and extending them back out to the sides in a controlled, rhythmic manner.
tips: Keep your movements smooth and controlled to maximize muscle activation and prevent injury.
Alternate which arm crosses over the other each time to ensure balanced muscle engagement.
Maintain an upright posture and engage your core to support your back and maintain balance.
results.description: Arm Double Crossover is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back.

results.name: Arm Pulses Cross
instructions: Stand tall with your back straight and feet shoulder-width apart.
Bring your forearms forward with your palms facing the floor and make a 90-degree angle with your upper arms.
Tighten your upper arms and move your hands towards each other.
As your one hand comes over the other one, return to the initial position and repeat.
tips: Engage your core to maintain stability and support your back throughout the exercise.
Keep your movements small and controlled to maximize muscle activation and prevent injury.
Focus on maintaining an even rhythm and alternating the crossover to ensure balanced muscle engagement.
results.description: Arm Pulses Cross is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back.

results.name: Arm Pulses Palms Downwards
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and your arms bent at the elbows, with your forearms parallel to the floor and palms facing upwards.
Perform small, quick pulses by moving your forearms forward and backward, maintaining the position and height.
Continue pulsing in a controlled, rhythmic manner for the desired duration or number of repetitions.
tips: Engage your core to maintain stability and support your back throughout the exercise.
Keep your shoulders relaxed and avoid tensing your neck and upper back.
Focus on maintaining a consistent pace and range of motion to ensure proper form.
results.description: Arm Pulses Palms Downwards is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back.

results.name: Arm Pulses Palms Upwards
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and your arms bent at the elbows, with your forearms parallel to the floor and palms facing downwards.
Perform small, quick pulses by moving your forearms forward and backward, maintaining the position and height.
Continue pulsing in a controlled, rhythmic manner for the desired duration or number of repetitions.
tips: Engage your core to maintain stability and support your back throughout the exercise.
Keep your shoulders relaxed and avoid tensing your neck and upper back.
Focus on maintaining a consistent pace and range of motion to ensure proper form.
results.description: Arm Pulses Palms Upwards is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back.

results.name: Arm Pulses
instructions: Stand tall with your back straight and feet shoulder-width apart.
Bend your arms to make a 90-degree angle with the elbows while keeping your palms facing inward.
Tighten your upper arms and move your arms forward and backward in a pulse-like fashion.
Keep doing this activity for a suitable time.
tips: Engage your core to maintain stability and support your back throughout the exercise.
Keep your movements small and controlled to maximize muscle activation and prevent injury.
Focus on keeping your shoulders relaxed and avoid tensing your neck and upper back.
results.description: Arm Pulses is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back.

results.name: Arms Lateral Raise and Rotation Up
instructions: Stand upright with your feet shoulder width apart, arms at your sides, and a slight bend in your elbows.
Raise your arms laterally until they reach shoulder height while rotating your shoulders so your palms face upward (supinated).
Rotate your arms at the shoulder joint so that your palms face down.
Slowly lower your arms to the starting position.
tips: Rotate your shoulders smoothly without forcing the range of motion.
Lift your arms under control and avoid using momentum.
Move only through a pain free range of motion.
Exhale as you raise your arms and inhale as you lower them.
results.description: Arms Lateral Raise and Rotation Up is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Traps, Serratus Anterior, Upper Back.

results.name: Arms Up and Down
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart. Extend your right arm straight up overhead and your left arm straight down by your side.
Simultaneously lower your right arm while raising your left arm, keeping both arms straight, until your right arm is down by your side and your left arm is overhead.
Continue alternating the arms in a controlled, rhythmic swinging motion, moving one arm up while the other moves down.
tips: Keep your movements smooth and rhythmic to enhance coordination and balance.
Use a steady breathing pattern, inhaling as you raise an arm and exhaling as you lower it.
Focus on extending through your fingertips to fully engage your shoulder and upper back muscles.
results.description: Arms Up and Down is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back.
